function: No learned PHY function: each hop's precoder comes from convex optimization (gradient descent, Algorithm 1) emulating an offline-trained image classifier, the application served (p. 1; p. 4).
notes: Page 1 holds the title of the DOI (Bian, Hua, Gunduz, 'Over-the-Air Inference Through Analog Computation Over Multi-Hop MIMO Networks', IEEE WCL 14(11), 2025). Reason no_learning. The physical-layer function is the precoder of each MIMO hop, and it is computed by a classical optimization: p. 1: "the precoding matrix for each hop is obtained by the corresponding relay terminal by solving an optimization problem, where the goal is to approximate the PrototypeNet weights with the effective channel matrix"; p. 4: "It is easy to show that the optimization problem is convex, and can be solved via gradient descent" (Algorithm 1). The learned element, PrototypeNet, is the image classifier (Fashion-MNIST, p. 4) whose inference the link computes over the air, so learning is the application that the link serves; the destination's learned FC layer outputs the image class (p. 2), it does not recover transmitted symbols. The federated-learning exception does not apply: p. 1: "we adopt offline centralized training to obtain the neural network weights", in contrast with training over the air. If the reviewer counts the channel-aware training of PrototypeNet (noise injection and power term in the loss, p. 3) as a learned physical-layer component, the next code that applies is function: over-the-air inference is not model aggregation across devices (area 7) and the precoders are not learned (area 3). Codes source_type, survey, system, and results do not apply: it is a research letter with simulation results (p. 4-5) and M = 49 antennas per node (p. 4).
